arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Brenan argued that a state court decision denying relief constitutes a merits ruling on the federal claim.
She stated this is especially true when the state court grapples with the substance of the alleged error.
Mr. Hermansen argued that the rule should follow the consensus of the courts of appeals.
He stated that courts look at the text of the reasoned opinion to determine what it says.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests when a state court decision counts as a merits ruling on a federal claim. the side that brought the case seeks federal habeas relief. the opposing side opposes that relief.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants the Supreme Court to treat the state court ruling as a merits decision on the federal claim.
the opposing side wants the Supreme Court to require an explicit statement that the state court resolved the federal claim.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues a state court decision denying relief implies a merits ruling unless the court states otherwise.
the opposing side argues courts must read the text of the opinion to determine if the federal claim was actually addressed.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Ginsburg asked if the argument was made under state law and then linked to the Sixth Amendment.
Justice Sotomayor asked if one can assume the state court reached the federal claim when it only discussed state evidentiary rules.

paragraphs: This dispute defines the scope of federal habeas review. It determines how state court rulings interact with federal constitutional claims. It affects the finality of state criminal judgments.
